description: An interactive sequencing activity where students arrange 8 shuffled stages of the water cycle into the correct order: from the Sun heating water through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff, and infiltration. Rebuilding the sequence from memory builds mastery of the complete cycle. Blue water-themed colour palette with Indian village monsoon setting in the background.
subject: Science
topic: The Water Cycle — Evaporation, Condensation, and Precipitation
chapter_reference: Chapter 7: Heat Transfer in Nature (Section 7.4 Water Cycle)

stages.title: Sun Heats Water Bodies
stages.description: The Sun heats water in oceans, rivers, and lakes.

stages.title: Water EVAPORATES
stages.description: Water turns into water vapour and rises.

stages.title: TRANSPIRATION from Plants
stages.description: Plants release water vapour through transpiration.

stages.title: Vapour CONDENSES
stages.description: Water vapour cools and forms clouds.

stages.title: PRECIPITATION Falls
stages.description: Clouds bring rain, snow, and hail.

stages.title: Water RUNOFF
stages.description: Rainwater flows over surface into water bodies.

stages.title: INFILTRATION into Ground
stages.description: Water seeps through soil into aquifers.

stages.title: Water Returns
stages.description: Water returns to oceans completing the cycle.

teaching_notes: Activate AFTER the water cycle video and diagram, as a self-test. Watch for common errors: transpiration placement, precipitation before condensation, and forgetting infiltration. After completion, ask: 'Where does Stage 8 connect back to Stage 1?' to reinforce the cyclical nature.
instructions_for_student: The 8 stages of the water cycle are all MIXED UP! Drag each stage into the correct position to rebuild the complete cycle from start to finish. Remember: the cycle begins with the Sun and ends with water returning to the ground. Can you get all 8 stages in the right order?
learning_objectives: Understand the complete water cycle process from solar heating to groundwater replenishment
Identify and sequence the key stages: evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff, and infiltration
Recognize that the water cycle is a continuous, never-ending loop
Learn key scientific terminology: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, transpiration, infiltration, runoff, aquifer
